title: Why Do Grapes Spark in a Microwave?

fin.big: Simplified illustrations. Do not try this at home.

parts: Cut a grape almost in half, put it in a microwave, and it can spark a tiny ball of plasma.
Do not try this. Stay for the real reason: the famous one is wrong.
The trick has been online for over twenty years.
The famous story? The thin strip of skin joining the halves acts like a tiny antenna.
In twenty nineteen, three physicists in Canada tested it.
They used two whole grapes. No skin bridge. They still sparked.
Then they swapped the grapes for beads of water gel. Same thing.
Not the skin, then. The real culprit hides inside every grape.
A grape-sized ball of water traps the microwaves inside it.
Put two together, and the energy piles up where they touch.
That tiny hotspot is where the plasma is born.
